• 85 Metal Bins for Public Areas: These durable metal bins will be strategically distributed throughout the village near dense concentration of households, industrial points…, and covering main streets and designated collection points.

properties.Full Activity Name: Supporting Maqneh community through the provision of a solar street lighting system and SWM equipment
properties.Activity Description:
150 solar street lighting units (incl. 20 spares) of 50 Watts each will be installed as part of the proposed project to meet all of the community's needs in Maqneh. According to estimates based on the existing halogen lamps, the old system's maintenance expenses and omission of electricity bills will result in annual savings of almost 24,000 USD.
The proposed intervention is aiming at supporting the municipality of Maqneh through the provision of a new 8-ton garbage compactor truck and 100 metal garbage bins to enable the municipality to perform the collection of solid waste adequately in the entire village, serving both Lebanese and Syrian communities. The requested garbage compactor truck is of a larger capacity than the existing vehicle, hence this vehicle would not only diminish the maintenance expenses, but it would also decrease the number of required trips to the sorting facility in Baalbek from 5 to 3 trips per week. Given that the new compactor will be fitted with a lifting device, the provision of 100 new metal garbage bins wil improves the garbage collection efficiency and saves the cost of replacing the old plastic bins that are being damaged or burned regularly.

properties.Full Activity Name: Provision of Solid Waste & infrastructure management equipment in support of Soultan Yacoub Municipality

Based on the findings, the intervention aims to provide the municipality with the following 1) a garbage compactor truck, 2) a backhoe loader with an extended Stick 3) a skid steer loader with a sweeper, 4) a tipper truck and 5) a bucket truck. properties.Full Activity Name: Supporting the agriculture cooperatives in Bint Jbeil village and GhanBatt AO
properties.Activity Description:
This priority intervention aims to support agricultural cooperatives in Bint Jbeil through the provision of essential equipment and machinery for agro-food production and processing. The agricultural sector in the area has been severely impacted by the recent conflict,which resulted in the destruction of critical farming tools, processing equipment, and storage units. Consequently, both cooperatives and individual farmers are experiencing serious challenges in maintaining their agricultural operations.
Beyond the physical destruction of assets, farmers have suffered substantial losses over the past two years due to the inability to cultivate or harvest their crops, resulting in the loss of multiple agricultural seasons. These compounded disruptions have jeopardized livelihoods, weakened food security, and eroded the economic resilience of farming communities. In response, the proposed project consists of supporting the livelihoods of farmers and re-strengthening the active agriculture cooperatives in Bint Jbeil through the provisions of equipment and tools. This project will enhance local value chains, improve productivity as well as contributing to community stabilization

properties.Full Activity Name: Provision of a jetting machine to clean the Septic tanks in Majdal Sellim
properties.Activity Description:
Majdal Sellim suffers from the complete absence of a public sewage network, leaving all residential units reliant on septic tanks for wastewater management. These tanks require regular emptying and maintenance to prevent public health risks, environmental contamination, and infrastructure degradation. The situation has been further exacerbated by the recent hostilities, which have increased the pressure on already fragile systems and highlighted the urgent need for improved sanitation services.
Currently, the municipality lacks the necessary equipment to provide adequate septic cleaning services, leading to delays, high service costs, and growing sanitation concerns. The provision of a septic truck with a jetting machine will significantly enhance the municipality’s capacity to ensure proper sanitation, reduce environmental and health hazards, and respond more effectively to post-conflict recovery needs.

properties.Full Activity Name: Supporting the vital sectors in Nabatiyeh through the provision of Renewable Energy

Targeted vital sectors are: (renewable energy)
Water well number 5 and 6 (lot 533) – Nabatieh Tahta
The water wells are located in Nabatieh and they benefit 6 main neighbourhoods, 30,000 residents and around 10,000 housing units. The wells are directly operated by SLWE with direct support from the municipality. Well number 5 has a flow of 110 m3 and well number 6 has a flow of 80 m3. The number of fixed-term employees at the culture center are 5.  The main problems facing the center are the lack of financial resources to secure the services and operational costs, especially the cost of energy and electricity.
As part of the sustainable intervention and to further support the quick operation of the center by being a critical and important facility in the area. This intervention will include equipping the center with furniture and equipment. The provision of equipment and furniture includes but is not limited to desks, chairs, ACs, printers, library closets, desktops, educational tools, projectors and flip charts.
Hassan Kamel Sabah sporting facility (lot 3940) – Nabatieh Tahta
The sporting facility is among the main public hubs across Nabatieh, especially since it matches the detailed specifications and measurements related to each stadium/hall. The facility contains one Basketball and Volleyball stadium, Karate Hall and one body building section. The facility is considered a main destination for the residents of Nabatieh and surroundings, especially youth groups.
Water well number 2 (lot 3090) – Nabatieh Al Fawka
The water well is located in Nabatieh Al Fawka and it benefits the majority of village, (around 800 housing units). The well is directly operated by SLWE with direct support from the municipality. Well number 2 has a flow of 35 m3 and its depth is around 450 meters. The main issue faced by SLWE and the municipality of Nabatieh al Fawka related to the water well is the high operation costs required to operate the wells within the multi-dimension crisis (securing fuel and maintenance costs).

properties.Full Activity Name: LAF Livelihood Ecosystem Project
properties.Activity Description:
The Lebanese Armed Forces (LAF) are and have remained the backbone of Lebanon’s security and stability and the most trusted institution by the people of Lebanon. With the violence halted, the LAF plays a critical role in ensuring the credible and timely implementation of the cessation of hostilities agreements, in responding to emergency crises, and conducting removal of unexploded ordnances operations. By supporting LAF personnel affected by the surge in violence, promoting the wellbeing of service members and their families, reducing negative coping mechanisms and ultimately fostering their capabilities, the LAF ecosystem initiative seeks to have a direct and lasting impact on the success of the LAF’s mission in laying the foundation for a sustainable and stable recovery process. The LAF Livelihood Ecosystem Project focuses on four main outputs toward achieving its objective:
Output 1: Enhancing the wellbeing and food security of LAF service members and their families;
The project is completing the construction of a temporary warehouse in Charles El Helou. The warehouse will serve as a main hub that will receive 13 different types of essential food products from the contracted FMCG supplier and redistribute them onto 64 LAF commissaries in BML that will be then sold to around 43,000 LAF service members at a 50% subsidy rate.
Additionally, the project is rehabilitating 3 LAF commissaries in BML to ensure the minimum work and healthy safety standards are all covered. These 3 commissaries (2 in Beirut and 1 in Keserwan-Jbeil governorate) serve around 3,750 service members.
Finally, under this output the project is also providing support to connect all 144 LAF commissaries to a central digital inventory and sales system managed by LAF central command. All 64 LAF commissaries located in BML are benefitting from this activity in addition to 15 LAF commissaries are benefitting from the provision of hardware and small equipment (such as POS machines, routers etc.) to ensure their main operations and connectivity to the central management system.
Output 2. Enhancing access to gender-sensitive quality social services to vulnerable LAF families;
As part of supporting the LAF livelihood ecosystem's different components, where securing service members' children's enrolment in schools is of vital importance amid the country's deteriorating socio-economic conditions, the project has covered the school tuition fees of 189 children with special needs of LAF service members located in BML for the Academic Year 2024-25. This output's intervention priorities are determined based on criteria taking into consideration the most urgent needs in the current country context.

properties.Full Activity Name: FPI1 - Mitigating the impact of conflict escalation in Lebanon on social, economic, and institutional stability - Crisis response & stabilization programme. Output 4.4: Support the Lebanon Mine Action Centre (LMAC)
properties.Activity Description: Within the current context, urgent mine action is critical for safeguarding communities in conflict-affected areas, as the presence of explosive ordnance presents immediate threats to safety and security. Without urgent intervention, civilian population, including vulnerable grouops such as women, children, and people with disabilities face immediate risks from the presence of explosvie ordnance contamination and lack of awareness thereof. UNDP will enhance its support to the Lebanon Mine Action Centre (LMAC), as the dedicated entity for mine action in Lebanon. UNDP will enhace its support to the LMAC to capacitate it to plan effectively, and act swiftly to address the contamination and support early recovery efforts, including rubble removal and mine clearance, leading to the safe return of IDPs. This will entail extensive advisory support to the insitution especially in terms of addressing the massive UXO threat, the procurement of needed equipment, particularly linked to debris/EOD and surveying material. UNDP will also support LMAC on data consolidation, and carrying out a review of newly contaminated areas. This will include provision of tools for information managmenet/data colleciton as well as coordination support, which is of particular importance in the current fluid/chaotic situation where access is a challenge.

properties.Full Activity Name: Addressing the Humanitarian and Development Impact Posed by Mines, Cluster Munitions and Explosive Remnants of War
properties.Activity Description:
The Lebanese community and the refugee community are suffering from a legacy contamination in Lebanon where a signigicant number of lands in the Bekaa, South, Mount Lebanon and other areas of Lebanon are still contaminated by landmines, cluster munitions and other explosvie remnants of war (ERW). The issue of contamination has been further compounded in 2017 following the defeat of terrorist groups in the North-Eastern border region that was contaminated mainly with improvised explosive devisces (EIDs). This proposed project focuses on empowering the Lebanon Mine Action Centre (LMAC) - the responsible body for the execution and coordination of the Lebanon Mine Action Programme (LMAP) on behalf of the Mine Action Authority - and enabling it to sustainably manage and address the humanitarian and development impact posed by mines, Explosive Remnants of War and Cluster Munitions. The overal objective is to significantly attentuate the impact of contamination risks through the promotion of resilient adaptable government institutions.
Among the activities completed so far:
1) Participation of LMAC in 13th Meeting of State Parties of the Convention on Cluster Munitions (CCM) in Geneva, 16-19 September, and CCM deadline for Lebanon extended till 2030.
2 ) Coordination Mechanism designed through workshop “Mine Action Coordination Gaps, Impacts & Suggested Solutions – Crisis Context” consisting of three different sessions was organized to pool in efforts for stakeholder coordination and the re-activation of the Inter-ministerial Committee. The participants included LMAC, LAF and operator NGOs (local and international).
3)  “Comprehensive Training on Management/Leadership, Communication/Public Speaking, Crisis Management” was completed between 22-25 Sept 2025 for all LMAC officers.
4) Provision of expertise and consultants to LMAC (Technical Advisor, NTS, social media)
5) Preparation of UNDP support to LMAC evaluation.
6) EOD and equipment being procured.
7) Upcoming Mine Action Forum being organised for 11 November 2025.
